front.title: Post-Quantum Rotation Envelope Semantic Scope and Differentiation

abstract.t: This document defines the semantic scope and differentiation of post-quantum rotation envelopes for X.509 certificate and key material. A rotation envelope carries the metadata that distinguishes a key rotation event from a fresh issuance, binding the new key to the predecessor it replaces and declaring the scope of objects (certificates, signatures, ciphertexts) whose trust transitions with the rotation. This document specifies the envelope structure and the differentiation rules that prevent rotation-envelope confusion across distinct rotation events.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: Post-quantum key rotation in X.509 -based systems is more complex than classical rotation: a single key may be used in multiple contexts (signature, key encapsulation, hybrid combiner), and the rotation of one component of a hybrid or composite key affects the trust of objects bound to that component. A rotation envelope captures the semantic scope of a rotation so that verifiers can determine which objects' trust transitions with the new key and which remain bound to the predecessor.

This section will describe the rotation-envelope concept and the differentiation problem: why distinct rotation events must not be conflatable, and how the envelope's semantic scope resolves ambiguity.

section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals as shown here.

section.name: Rotation Envelope Structure
section.t: This section will define the envelope structure: the predecessor key identifier, the successor key identifier, the rotation timestamp, the scope declaration (which object classes and contexts transition), and the signature binding the envelope to the rotating authority. The structure will be expressed as an X.509 extension or a standalone signed object, with ASN.1 syntax.

section.name: Semantic Scope Declaration
section.t: This section will define the semantic scope declaration: the set of object classes (certificates, CRLs, OCSP responses, signed messages, encapsulated keys) whose trust transitions with the rotation, and the contexts (e.g., signature-only versus key-encapsulation) in which the transition applies. The section will specify how a verifier interprets the scope when evaluating an object bound to a rotated key.

section.name: Differentiation Rules
section.t: This section will define the differentiation rules that prevent confusion between distinct rotation events: each envelope carries a unique rotation identifier, a monotonic sequence number within the rotating authority, and a hash binding to the predecessor envelope. The section will specify the verification procedure that detects duplicate, reordered, or substituted envelopes.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: This section will analyze threats to rotation envelopes: envelope forgery (inducing a verifier to trust a successor not actually rotated by the authority), scope over-extension (claiming a broader transition than the authority intended), and rollback (reverting to a predecessor by suppressing the envelope). The section will identify the mitigations provided by the envelope structure and differentiation rules.
